title: The A-Road Collision
briefing: A Valtren driver on a 10-hour route clipped a barrier at 02:40. He is unhurt; the load is lost. The tachograph shows he was within legal limits but had worked six nights straight.
The Fleet Manager asks the risk team to lead the review.

evidence.title: Tachograph summary
evidence.body: Within daily limits. Six consecutive night shifts. Rest periods at the legal minimum each day.

evidence.title: Route data
evidence.body: Long-route share has stayed amber for four weeks. Night routes over 9 hours: 31% of night shifts.

evidence.title: Driver statement
evidence.body: "I was tired. Everyone's covering for the shortage."

questions.prompt: What is the main cause to address?

options.label: Rostering that keeps drivers legal but fatigued: legal limits are not the same as safe limits
options.feedback: The control (legal limits) was met; the risk (fatigue) wasn't controlled.

options.label: The driver kept driving while tired instead of stopping, which the fatigue policy already requires
options.feedback: He told you why: the roster.

options.label: A badly placed roadside barrier on a route the drivers say is poorly lit at night

questions.prompt: What do you recommend straight away?

options.label: A fatigue rule above the legal minimum: at most four nights in a row, no night route over 9 hours
options.feedback: Closes the gap between legal and safe.

options.label: A formal reminder to all drivers of the duty to stop when tired, with the collision as the example
options.feedback: Punishes the symptom and silences the next report.

options.label: No change until the investigation is complete: he was within the legal limits
options.feedback: Legal compliance didn't prevent the collision.

questions.prompt: The long-route KRI was amber for four weeks. What failed?

options.label: Nobody acted on the amber: the escalation rule was not followed
options.feedback: The indicator worked; the response didn't.

options.label: The KRI measured route length rather than hours actually driven, so it missed the real exposure
Amber was set too close to normal, so a real warning looked like the usual noise
options.feedback: It was amber, and correctly so.

options.label: What happened, what changes now, and how to raise fatigue concerns without consequences
A safety bulletin reminding drivers to take breaks and use the fatigue policy
options.feedback: Puts the burden back on the driver.

options.label: Nothing until the review is finished, to avoid speculation about the driver involved and his record

lesson: Legal limits are a floor, not a safety control. Act on amber indicators, fix the system that made fatigue normal, and protect the people who tell you.

escalation.text: Nobody from risk picked up "The A-Road Collision" in time. The executive team handled it alone, late and without a plan, and the damage spread.
